edges.mechanism: Monacolin K is lovastatin; adding RYR to a statin duplicates HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor exposure and myopathy/hepatotoxicity risk. EU labeling forbids use with cholesterol-lowering medication.
edges.evidence: EFSA opinions; EU Regulation 2022/860; RCTs of RYR+statin show little added LDL-C benefit

edges.with: strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (clarithromycin, itraconazole/azole antifungals, HIV protease inhibitors)
edges.mechanism: CYP3A4 inhibition raises lovastatin/lovastatin acid exposure (itraconazole >20-fold AUC; clarithromycin >5-fold), raising rhabdomyolysis risk; extrapolated to monacolin K.
edges.evidence: Crossover PK RCT with lovastatin; systematic review of clarithromycin-statin cases; no RYR-specific PK study

edges.mechanism: Intestinal CYP3A4 inhibition; double-strength grapefruit juice raised lovastatin AUC 15-fold and lovastatin acid AUC 5-fold.
edges.evidence: Randomized crossover PK study with lovastatin (n=10); extrapolated to monacolin K

edges.mechanism: Gemfibrozil raised lovastatin acid concentrations with an RYR product; lovastatin-gemfibrozil caused severe myopathy/rhabdomyolysis (median CK 15,250 U/L).
edges.evidence: Volunteer PK study with RYR; FDA case series with lovastatin

edges.mechanism: CYP3A4/transporter interaction raises monacolin/lovastatin exposure; rhabdomyolysis in a renal transplant recipient on cyclosporine taking RYR.
edges.evidence: Case report; mechanistic PK data with lovastatin

edges.mechanism: Garlic antiplatelet activity may add to anticoagulation; case reports of enhanced anticoagulant effect, but an RCT of aged garlic extract with warfarin found no increase in bleeding.
edges.evidence: Pilot RCT (n=48), reviews; low certainty

edges.mechanism: Garlic inhibits platelet aggregation in vitro and in about half of RCTs; additive effect with platelet inhibitors unstudied.
edges.evidence: Systematic review of 12 RCTs; mechanistic studies; dietary-dose RCT negative

edges.mechanism: Garlic supplements reduced saquinavir AUC 51% and trough 49%, risking loss of antiviral efficacy.
edges.evidence: Open-label PK study in 10 volunteers

edges.mechanism: Garlic lowers SBP/DBP by about 4/3 mmHg in hypertension; small additive BP lowering.
edges.evidence: Meta-analyses of RCTs

edges.mechanism: Garlic antiplatelet effect may add to aspirin's; NCCIH advises discussing garlic with aspirin use.
edges.evidence: Agency guidance plus RCT systematic review; interaction not quantified

edges.mechanism: Berberine (PCSK9-related) plus RYR are co-formulated; combination lowers LDL-C (MD -18.79 mg/dL) more than berberine alone.
edges.evidence: Meta-analyses of RCTs (Armolipid Plus and berberine combinations)

edges.mechanism: HMG-CoA reductase inhibition by RYR depleted tissue CoQ10 in mice; RYR+CoQ10 combination tested in an RCT; benefit for myalgia unproven.
edges.evidence: Animal study plus RCT of combination

edges.mechanism: Duplicate garlic exposure: additive antiplatelet and BP-lowering effects and more odor/GI effects.
edges.evidence: Meta-analyses and adverse-effect review

edges.mechanism: Kyolic is aged garlic extract; stacking duplicates AGE antiplatelet and BP effects.
edges.evidence: AGE meta-analysis and mechanistic platelet study

edges.mechanism: Fish oil and garlic both have reported bleeding risks; additive effect plausible perioperatively.
edges.evidence: Narrative review of supplements and coagulation

edges.mechanism: Ginger and garlic are both reported to affect platelet function/bleeding; evidence for warfarin interaction weak.
edges.evidence: Reviews

edges.mechanism: Green tea extract and red yeast rice are both among the 6 botanicals most often implicated in US herbal hepatotoxicity; green tea also has reported bleeding risk.
edges.evidence: NHANES exposure study of hepatotoxic botanicals; coagulation review

edges.mechanism: Turmeric and red yeast rice are both among the most frequently reported hepatotoxic botanicals; stacking adds liver-injury exposure.
edges.evidence: NHANES-based review of hepatotoxic botanicals

edges.mechanism: Turmeric/curcumin and red yeast rice are both among the most frequently reported hepatotoxic botanicals; stacking adds liver-injury exposure.
edges.evidence: NHANES-based review of hepatotoxic botanicals

edges.mechanism: Monacolin K is lovastatin; no safety studies; NCCIH advises against use and EU labels prohibit use in pregnant or lactating women.
edges.evidence: Agency guidance and EU regulation

edges.with: liver disease or prior statin hepatotoxicity
edges.mechanism: RYR shows hepatic disproportionality signals (FAERS ROR 13.71) and caused biopsy-proven hepatitis after prior lovastatin hepatotoxicity.
edges.evidence: Pharmacovigilance and case reports; EFSA opinion

edges.mechanism: Citrinin nephrotoxicity; puberulic-acid-contaminated beni-koji caused Fanconi syndrome and persistent eGFR loss; rhabdomyolysis with AKI in transplant recipient.
edges.evidence: Product analyses, nationwide survey (n=192), case reports

edges.mechanism: Garlic antiplatelet effects; excess surgical bleeding reported with high garlic intake; ASA/AANA advise stopping herbal medicines 1-2 weeks pre-op.
edges.evidence: Case report and perioperative review

edges.with: creatine kinase and liver enzymes (CK, ALT/AST)
edges.mechanism: True physiological rises with statin-like myotoxicity/hepatotoxicity (myalgia/CK rises, rhabdomyolysis with CK >100,000 U/L, ALT/AST elevations).
edges.evidence: Pharmacovigilance series, case reports, umbrella review

edges.mechanism: Reduced OATP1B1 hepatic uptake raises lovastatin acid AUC (~2.9-fold) and statin myopathy risk; extrapolated to monacolin K.
edges.evidence: Genotype-panel PK study with lovastatin; GWAS; CPIC guideline
